title: DiffDock: SE(3) Diffusion Generative Modeling Transforms Blind Protein–Ligand Molecular Docking
whyItMatters: Reframed protein–ligand molecular docking from brittle energy-scoring optimization into a diffusion generative process over ligand translations, rotations, and torsions—doubling blind-docking accuracy on PDBBind.
summary: Published at ICLR 2023 (arXiv October 2022, revised February 2023) by Gabriele Corso, Hannes Stärk, Bowen Jing, Regina Barzilay, and Tommi Jaakkola at MIT, DiffDock reframed blind protein–ligand docking as a generative modeling problem on the product manifold of 3D translations, SO(3) rotations, and rotatable torsion angles. Paired with a learned confidence model, DiffDock achieved 38% top-1 success (<2 Å RMSD) on the PDBBind blind-docking benchmark—nearly doubling the accuracy of prior deep-learning models (23%) and physics-based search engines like AutoDock Vina and GNINA (20–23%)—while showing far greater robustness on computationally predicted (ESMFold) protein structures.
technicalHighlights: Defined a score-based diffusion generative process over the non-Euclidean manifold of ligand poses (translation, SO(3) rotation, and internal torsion angles).
Achieved 38.2% top-1 (<2 Å) blind-docking success on PDBBind, nearly doubling prior deep-learning and classical physics-based docking methods.
Pioneered generative diffusion for protein–small-molecule complex prediction, directly paving the conceptual bridge toward all-atom co-folding models like AlphaFold 3 and Boltz-2.
caveats: Later community benchmarks (PoseBusters) revealed that DiffDock poses could occasionally violate physical stereochemical constraints (steric clashes or bond lengths), motivating physics-aware energy checks and co-folding architectures.

scoreRationale.foundational: Shifted computational drug docking from deterministic energy-minimization search to geometric generative diffusion over molecular degrees of freedom.
scoreRationale.ripple: Became one of the most widely adopted open-source docking tools and directly influenced diffusion-based co-folding (AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, Chai).
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed at ICLR 2023 with open-source weights and extensive independent benchmarking (including PoseBusters audits).
scoreRationale.velocity: Delivered accurate blind docking across whole protein surfaces in seconds without prior binding-pocket specification.
